tierReasons.fact: S2.5-01b adds organization-owned removal admission, current authority and exact target checks, last-active-Admin protection, and conditional completion. The existing private SQL adapter implements a new public RemovalOperationStore on the same bounded pool, with one pending operation per organization and retained terminal receipts. Uncertain effects remain held without replay. A 30-second owner lifetime and ten-page bound guard dispatch; optional neutral read signals stop further WorkOS read substeps while in-flight calls retain their existing five-second timeout. App supplies and closes the removal owner before shared SQL. Public request/result/store and directory stop contracts are snapshot-visible; invitation results and unrelated callers stay compatible. Organizations and audit-logs gain responsibilities and shared storage/recovery guarantees change, but the component set, source dependency pairs, C4 container topology, provider selection, and runtime configuration remain. Updated registry views describe the new runtime call separately from the existing opposite type dependency. No browser removal route, customer removal export, MFA, or live migration is added. The policy change registers the new public module and extends the existing PostgreSQL gate without weakening checks.

policyAnswers.protected_paths.policy: The policy registers the new public RemovalOperationStore and extends the existing real-PostgreSQL gate with removal/settings coverage. No gate, approval decision or failure criterion is weakened. Three new-file MI exceptions retain explicit bounded reasons through 2026-12-24; independent human review stays required. Habit snooze stays empty.
policyAnswers.protected_paths.contracts: Internal removeMember(actor, request) adds exact organization/membership/revision inputs and bounded denied/stale/unsupported/last-admin/busy/unavailable/unknown/applied outcomes. Durable per-organization admission has no lease or replay. An uncertain completion is accepted only after an exact matching terminal receipt. Optional directory signals stop later WorkOS read substeps while in-flight requests keep their existing timeout. Existing callers can omit the signal. No browser removal action or customer removal Audit capture is added.
policyAnswers.deployment_and_recovery: Before activation an owner applies the additive membership_removal_operations migration. The existing concrete SQL store/pool owns both settings and removal intent; no startup migration, environment variable, key, provider, paid service or deployment/container change is added. Keep pending operations through restart and application rollback. Database restore safety is not proved; elapsed time or current provider reads cannot clear a hold. Independent reconciliation and restore safety stay in the runbook work.
policyAnswers.sensitive_behavior: Current actor Admin authority precedes admission and is checked again with exact target revision/status/ordinary management, all raw target grants and complete bounded active pages. Later duplicate membership facts win, and the last usable active Admin cannot be removed. One single exact-ID dispatch can occur only before stop; uncertainty holds without replay. Recording failure cannot change the result. R1 remains open and no improvement to email-read cost is claimed.
policyAnswers.dependencies_and_architecture: No npm dependency key, Node builtin import, component set or source owner pair is added. Existing organizations and audit-logs responsibilities gain durable removal calls over the same store. Runtime organization-to-store calls are distinct from the existing opposite type dependency. Registry drawings change; actual component/container topology and provider choice remain. No ADR was requested by an authorized decision maker.
policyAnswers.approval_and_scope: User directly attests independent architect approval of the full Slice2.5 stack. Record it as user attestation; this worker invents no reviewer identity, GitHub review or timestamp. Manager owns final candidate mapping, gate results, hold reconciliation and merge decisions. No commit, push, live migration or deployment is performed by this worker.
